name: What is the difference between a whole house remodel and a home addition?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a whole house remodel and a home addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A whole house remodel primarily focuses on renovating existing spaces within your home's current footprint, updating aesthetics, functionality, or structural integrity. This might involve reconfiguring interior layouts or upgrading finishes. A home addition, on the other hand, involves expanding your home's square footage by building new structures, such as adding a second story, new rooms, or extending existing ones. While a remodel improves what's already there, an addition creates new habitable space, often requiring more extensive planning and permits.
acceptedAnswer.description: A whole house remodel updates existing spaces, while a home addition expands your home's square footage by building new structures.
